title: I-SplineFlow: Learning Monotone Spline Stochastic Interpolant Schedulers for Few-Step Generation

paper.title: I-SplineFlow: Learning Monotone Spline Stochastic Interpolant Schedulers for Few-Step Generation
paper.abstract:
Abstract Few-step generation with pretrained diffusion and flow models can be accelerated
by lightweight training that optimizes the sampling trajectory rather than the
network. A recent approach parameterizes the stochastic interpolant (SI)
scheduler as a smooth curve whose control points enforce the three properties an
SI scheduler must satisfy: fixed boundary conditions, a monotone
signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and differentiability. Existing parameterizations
use globally supported polynomial bases, where every control point moves the
whole curve and higher expressiveness needs a higher degree, which couples
distant regions of the schedule during optimization. We introduce I-SplineFlow , which parameterizes the scheduler with integrated monotone
splines (I-splines). I-splines decouple the polynomial degree from the number of
mixture weights, so support width and smoothness can be chosen per model at a
fixed weight count, and the compactly supported derivative basis makes the
scheduler Jacobian orders of magnitude better conditioned than a Bézier basis.
Boundary conditions and a strictly monotone SNR hold by construction, with no
ordering constraint on the parameters and closed-form velocity derivatives.
Across diffusion (EDM) and flow (ReFlow, Simple ReFlow) models, I-SplineFlow
improves few-step FID over Bézier scheduling in most settings, most clearly at
the lowest NFEs, and trains in minutes. Ablations show that both the degree
freedom and the monotonicity constraint are needed. The code will be released upon acceptance.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Diffusion and flow-based generative models achieve state-of-the-art sample quality, but iterative sampling incurs a high number of function evaluations (NFEs) ( Ho, Jain, and Abbeel 2020 ; Song et al. 2021 ; Lipman et al. 2023 ) . Acceleration ranges from dedicated ODE solvers ( Lu et al. 2022 ; Zhao et al. 2023 ; Zhang and Chen 2023 ) to distillation ( Song et al. 2023 ; Liu, Gong, and Liu 2023 ) , the latter costing hundreds to thousands of GPU hours. The lightweight training paradigm instead freezes the pretrained model and learns a small set of parameters under a fixed NFE budget. Most methods learn a nondecreasing sequence of ODE timesteps ( Tong et al. 2025 ; Chen et al. 2024 ; Xue et al. 2024 ) . Min et al. 2026 instead learn the sampling path by parameterizing the stochastic interpolant (SI) scheduler ( Albergo, Boffi, and Vanden-Eijnden 2023 ) , which transforms the trajectory geometry while preserving the endpoint marginals and the frozen network. An SI scheduler must satisfy three properties: fixed boundary conditions, a monotone SNR so the induced time map is invertible, and differentiability. Min et al. 2026 meet these with a Bézier parameterization, but the Bernstein basis is globally supported : its degree is tied to the control-point count ( degree = K − 1 \text{degree}=K-1 ), so raising expressiveness raises the degree, which couples distant regions of the schedule and conditions the optimization poorly. We introduce I-SplineFlow , which replaces the Bézier basis with integrated monotone splines (I-splines). Our contributions are: 1. Freedom of degree and control points. A spline basis decouples the polynomial degree p p from the number of mixture weights K K : on a clamped knot vector K = p + 1 + m K=p+1+m with m m interior knots, so at fixed K K the degree trades against interior knots and raising it adds no learnable parameters. The derivative (M-spline) basis is compactly supported, so each weight controls the signal/noise density over only a few knot spans, giving local control of the scheduler derivative that a globally supported Bézier basis does not offer. (The integral I i I_{i} is not compactly supported and the softmax couples the weights, so coupling in the scheduler value is reduced, not eliminated.) 2. Monotonicity by construction. I-splines are non-negative, monotone basis functions with fixed endpoints, so a non-negative (softmax) mixture yields a strictly monotone SNR and exact boundary conditions automatically, with no ordering constraint on the raw parameters. All scheduler derivatives for the transformed velocity remain in closed form, meeting the differentiability requirement at the C 2 C^{2} smoothness the scheduler needs. 3. Local support gives better-conditioned optimization. The compactly supported derivative basis produces a banded parameter coupling and a scheduler Jacobian orders of magnitude better conditioned than the Bézier basis (Figure 5 ). This is a property of the basis, not the optimizer, and holds without value-locality, which neither method has; empirically the better-conditioned landscape trains faster at a matched budget. With both properties in place, I-SplineFlow improves few-step FID over Bézier scheduling in most settings across diffusion and flow models, most clearly at low NFE, and trains in minutes. An otherwise-identical non-monotone B-spline variant degrades sharply and can diverge on wide-SNR diffusion schedules, which isolates monotonicity as the operative property.

sections.heading: Learning ODE timesteps.
sections.text: Several lightweight methods optimize the sequence of solver timesteps under a fixed budget: allocating steps to high-curvature regions ( Chen et al. 2024 ) , minimizing accumulated integration error ( Xue et al. 2024 ) , or learning timesteps by teacher-forcing distillation ( Tong et al. 2025 ) . All optimize discrete per-step variables on a fixed path and generalize poorly to unseen NFEs.

sections.heading: Learning sampling trajectories.
sections.text: A second line changes the trajectory itself. Some works select among predefined SI schedulers at inference ( Karras et al. 2022 ; Pokle et al. 2024 ) ; Shaul et al. 2024 learn a target path with a discrete per-step parameterization that models values and derivatives separately, which destabilizes optimization. Closest to us, Min et al. 2026 learn a continuous SI scheduler via Bézier curves; we adopt this constraint-by-construction approach and target the global support of the Bernstein basis, which ties degree to control-point count.

sections.heading: Learning solver coefficients.
sections.text: A complementary direction learns the solver’s aggregation weights ( Zhao et al. 2026 ) with unconstrained, time-varying parameters that relax the sum-to-one constraint. We instead parameterize the scheduler and argue that an explicit monotonicity constraint helps; we include this comparison for context and do not evaluate against it.

sections.heading: Scheduler parameterizations.
sections.text: Learned noise schedules also appear in variational diffusion models ( Kingma et al. 2023 ) , which model the log-SNR with a monotone network ( > 10 3 >\!10^{3} parameters), and multi-marginal interpolants ( Albergo et al. 2024 ) , whose trigonometric parameterization does not guarantee a monotone SNR. Our I-spline parameterization is compact and satisfies all three requirements by construction.

sections.heading: Requirements and the Limitation of Global Bases
sections.text: An admissible scheduler must satisfy: (i) boundary conditions (endpoints fixed), (ii) monotonicity of the SNR ρ ¯ \bar{\rho} (so that ( 3 ) is invertible), and (iii) differentiability (so that ( 4 ) is well defined; in practice C 2 C^{2} ). The Bézier parameterization ( Min et al. 2026 ) satisfies all three via K K ordered control points. But the Bernstein basis is globally supported : for an n n -degree curve with n + 1 n{+}1 control points, B ⁡ ( λ ) = ∑ i = 0 n b i , n ​ ( λ ) ​ C i , b i , n ​ ( λ ) = ( n i ) ​ ( 1 − λ ) n − i ​ λ i , B(\lambda)=\sum_{i=0}^{n}b_{i,n}(\lambda)\,C_{i},\quad b_{i,n}(\lambda)=\binom{n}{i}(1-\lambda)^{n-i}\lambda^{i}, (6) each b i , n b_{i,n} is nonzero on the whole interval ( 0 , 1 ) (0,1) . Two consequences follow. First, the polynomial degree is coupled to the control-point count ( n = K − 1 n=K-1 ): more control points force higher degree. Second, every control point perturbs the entire curve, so optimization cannot adjust one region of the schedule without affecting all others.

sections.heading: I-Spline Stochastic Interpolant Scheduler
sections.text: We parameterize each scheduler coefficient with integrated monotone splines (I-splines), which resolve both issues.

sections.heading: The Role of Monotonicity: a Controlled Ablation
sections.text: To isolate which of the two properties drives performance, we introduce a B-spline counterpart. It shares the entire basis machinery, knots, degree, and initialization of the I-spline, so it keeps the degree/control-point freedom of Contribution 1, but it replaces the non-negative I-spline mixture with free control points, α ¯ θ ​ ( s ) = ∑ i c i ( α ) ​ N i , p ​ ( s ) , c 0 ( α ) = 0 , c K − 1 ( α ) = 1 , \bar{\alpha}_{\theta}(s)=\sum_{i}c_{i}^{(\alpha)}N_{i,p}(s),\quad c_{0}^{(\alpha)}{=}0,\ c_{K-1}^{(\alpha)}{=}1, (10) so the curve is not constrained to be monotone. Comparing B-spline to I-spline under identical settings probes the effect of monotonicity (Contribution 2); comparing B-spline to Bézier probes degree/control-point decoupling (Contribution 1). sections.heading: Experiments
sections.text: We evaluate on diffusion and flow models. For diffusion, EDM ( Karras et al. 2022 ) on CIFAR-10 ( 32 × 32 32{\times}32 ), FFHQ and AFHQv2 ( 64 × 64 64{\times}64 ), with UniPC ( Zhao et al. 2023 ) and iPNDM ( Zhang and Chen 2023 ) . For flow, ReFlow ( Liu, Gong, and Liu 2023 ) and Simple ReFlow ( Kim et al. 2025 ) on CIFAR-10 and FlowDCN ( Wang et al. 2024 ) on ImageNet ( 256 × 256 256{\times}256 ), with RK1 (Euler) and RK2 (Midpoint). Following BézierFlow ( Min et al. 2026 ) , teachers use a high-order adaptive solver from shared noise and we train an LPIPS objective on matched budgets (200 pairs for CIFAR-10, 50 otherwise). All runs use K = 32 K{=}32 and RMSprop; FID uses 50K samples against the EDM reference statistics.

sections.heading: Diffusion models.
sections.text: I-SplineFlow achieves the best FID in most settings across the three datasets and beats BézierFlow in every column on CIFAR-10 (UniPC), FFHQ (UniPC), and AFHQv2 (both solvers), as shown in Table . With iPNDM the gain concentrates at the lowest NFEs (6.47 vs. 6.53 on CIFAR-10, 12.35 vs. 13.89 on AFHQv2 at NFE = 4 {=}4 ), where discretization error dominates.

sections.heading: Flow models.
sections.text: On ReFlow, I-SplineFlow is best in every column, with the largest low-NFE gains under RK2 (5.35 vs. 6.03 at NFE=6). On the near-straight ReFlow++ trajectories all methods sit within a narrow band, yet I-SplineFlow still attains the best FID at every NFE. On ImageNet with FlowDCN it leads at NFE 6–10; at NFE 4 Bespoke is lowest, where the curved high-resolution trajectory favors a per-step solver. Degree 3 suffices throughout, since little curvature remains to fit.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: We introduced I-SplineFlow, which parameterizes the stochastic interpolant scheduler with integrated monotone splines. The I-spline basis decouples the polynomial degree from the number of control points and enforces boundary conditions and a monotone SNR by construction, with no ordering constraint on the parameters and closed-form derivatives for the transformed velocity. Trained in minutes on a frozen pretrained model, it improves few-step FID over Bézier-based scheduling in most settings, with the clearest gains at the lowest NFEs. The gains are strongest on flow-based models, where I-SplineFlow attains the best FID in every reported setting, and more mixed on diffusion models. Closing that gap is the natural next step: we plan to explore other spline bases that hold up better across diffusion schedules.

A recent approach parameterizes the stochastic interpolant (SI) scheduler as a smooth curve whose control points enforce the three properties an SI scheduler must satisfy: fixed boundary conditions, a monotone signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and differentiability. Existing parameterizations use globally supported polynomial bases, where every control point moves the whole curve and higher expressiveness needs a higher degree, which couples distant regions of the schedule during optimization. We introduce I-SplineFlow , which parameterizes the scheduler with integrated monotone splines (I-splines). I-splines decouple the polynomial degree from the number of mixture weights, so support width and smoothness can be chosen per model at a fixed weight count, and the compactly supported derivative basis makes the scheduler Jacobian orders of magnitude better conditioned than a Bézier basis. Boundary conditions and a strictly monotone SNR hold by construction, with no ordering constraint on the parameters and closed-form velocity derivatives. Across diffusion (EDM) and flow (ReFlow, Simple ReFlow) models, I-SplineFlow improves few-step FID over Bézier scheduling in most settings, most clearly at the lowest NFEs, and trains in minutes. Ablations show that both the degree freedom and the monotonicity constraint are needed. The code will be released upon acceptance. Introduction Diffusion and flow-based generative models achieve state-of-the-art sample quality, but iterative sampling incurs a high number of function evaluations (NFEs) ( Ho, Jain, and Abbeel 2020 ; Song et al. 2021 ; Lipman et al. 2023 ) . Acceleration ranges from dedicated ODE solvers ( Lu et al. 2022 ; Zhao et al. 2023 ; Zhang and Chen 2023 ) to distillation ( Song et al. 2023 ; Liu, Gong, and Liu 2023 ) , the latter costing hundreds to thousands of GPU hours. The lightweight training paradigm instead freezes the pretrained model and learns a small set of parameters under a fixed NFE budget. Most methods learn a nondecreasing sequence of ODE timesteps ( Tong et al. 2025 ; Chen et al. 2024 ; Xue et al. 2024 ) . Min et al. 2026 instead learn the sampling path by parameterizing the stochastic interpolant (SI) scheduler ( Albergo, Boffi, and Vanden-Eijnden 2023 ) , which transforms the trajectory geometry while preserving the endpoint marginals and the frozen network. An SI scheduler must satisfy three properties: fixed boundary conditions, a monotone SNR so the induced time map is invertible, and differentiability. Min et al. 2026 meet these with a Bézier parameterization, but the Bernstein basis is globally supported : its degree is tied to the control-point count ( degree = K − 1 \text{degree}=K-1 ), so raising expressiveness raises the degree, which couples distant regions of the schedule and conditions the optimization poorly. We introduce I-SplineFlow , which replaces the Bézier basis with integrated monotone splines (I-splines). Our contributions are: 1. Freedom of degree and control points. A spline basis decouples the polynomial degree p p from the number of mixture weights K K : on a clamped knot vector K = p + 1 + m K=p+1+m with m m interior knots, so at fixed K K the degree trades against interior knots and raising it adds no learnable parameters. The derivative (M-spline) basis is compactly supported, so each weight controls the signal/noise density over only a few knot spans, giving local control of the scheduler derivative that a globally supported Bézier basis does not offer. (The integral I i I_{i} is not compactly supported and the softmax couples the weights, so coupling in the scheduler value is reduced, not eliminated.) 2. Monotonicity by construction. I-splines are non-negative, monotone basis functions with fixed endpoints, so a non-negative (softmax) mixture yields a strictly monotone SNR and exact boundary conditions automatically, with no ordering constraint on the raw parameters. Local support gives better-conditioned optimization. The compactly supported derivative basis produces a banded parameter coupling and a scheduler Jacobian orders of magnitude better conditioned than the Bézier basis (Figure 5 ). This is a property of the basis, not the optimizer, and holds without value-locality, which neither method has; empirically the better-conditioned landscape trains faster at a matched budget. With both properties in place, I-SplineFlow improves few-step FID over Bézier scheduling in most settings across diffusion and flow models, most clearly at low NFE, and trains in minutes. An otherwise-identical non-monotone B-spline variant degrades sharply and can diverge on wide-SNR diffusion schedules, which isolates monotonicity as the operative property. Related Work Learning ODE timesteps. Several lightweight methods optimize the sequence of solver timesteps under a fixed budget: allocating steps to high-curvature regions ( Chen et al. 2024 ) , minimizing accumulated integration error ( Xue et al. 2024 ) , or learning timesteps by teacher-forcing distillation ( Tong et al. 2025 ) . All optimize discrete per-step variables on a fixed path and generalize poorly to unseen NFEs. Learning sampling trajectories. A second line changes the trajectory itself. Some works select among predefined SI schedulers at inference ( Karras et al. 2022 ; Pokle et al. 2024 ) ; Shaul et al. 2024 learn a target path with a discrete per-step parameterization that models values and derivatives separately, which destabilizes optimization. Closest to us, Min et al. 2026 learn a continuous SI scheduler via Bézier curves; we adopt this constraint-by-construction approach and target the global support of the Bernstein basis, which ties degree to control-point count. Learning solver coefficients. A complementary direction learns the solver’s aggregation weights ( Zhao et al. 2026 ) with unconstrained, time-varying parameters that relax the sum-to-one constraint. We instead parameterize the scheduler and argue that an explicit monotonicity constraint helps; we include this comparison for context and do not evaluate against it. Scheduler parameterizations. Learned noise schedules also appear in variational diffusion models ( Kingma et al. 2023 ) , which model the log-SNR with a monotone network ( > 10 3 >\!10^{3} parameters), and multi-marginal interpolants ( Albergo et al. 2024 ) , whose trigonometric parameterization does not guarantee a monotone SNR. Our I-spline parameterization is compact and satisfies all three requirements by construction.
